rule: Sovereign Cloud Advisory placement ladder (PLAN S7, D17, D19). Rungs are cumulative: a kind of data needs every control of its minimum rung and of the rungs below it. The minimum rung is the one whose level equals the data's required level. A 'platformMove' rung cannot be reached in a provider's standard regions when the provider's parent is outside the data's allowed zone: the data moves to an offering at that rung (LTM judgement, owner approval at Gate S7; counsel confirms R4 at S10). The ladder changes the advice, never the maturity score (D3). Options are examples of service families, each sourced in the claims register with a review date; they are listed in a fixed order that does not rank providers.

rungs.label: Standard region
rungs.means: Any standard region; no sovereignty controls required

rungs.label: In-zone region with guardrails
rungs.means: A standard region inside the allowed zone, with policies that block deployments elsewhere; backups and replicas in the zone too

rungs.label: Customer-held keys and approved access
rungs.means: R1, plus keys held outside the provider, provider access only with your approval, and the provider's data boundary where one exists

rungs.label: Sovereign offering run in the zone
rungs.means: R2, plus a service operated and supported only by staff in the zone, employed by a local entity under local law

rungs.label: Out of foreign-law reach, or disconnected
rungs.means: R3, plus no provider in the chain can be compelled by a law from outside the zone, or the system is disconnected
